Counsel for Applicant :- Abhishek Singh,Narendra Kumar Pandey

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned AGA for the State and perused the record.
2. The applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.16 of 2023, under Section 376-AB, 504 IPC and Section 5M/6 of POCSO Act at P.S. Maurawan, District -Unnao.
3. The FIR in question was lodged initially under Sections 354, 352, 504 read with Section 9/10 of the POCSO Act.

The FIR was lodged alleging that the daughter of the informant, aged about 5 years,
had gone out to play but did not come.
When she came home and was asked, she informed that the applicant, who is 75 years of age, misbehaved with her.

In the Statements under Section 161 Cr.P.C.,
the victim stated that the applicant took her to his home and tried to misbehave with her.

However,
in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she leveled allegations to constitute the offence under Indar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home, ... on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23993431/
1 Section 376 IPC read with Section 5M/6 of POCSO Act.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The medical on record does not corroborate the version and indicates that no injury was seen on the external and the private part of the victim.

In the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., it is also stated that the victim, aged about five years,
was flying a kite when the incident occurred.
4. Learned counsel for applicant argues that there is a history of litigation in between the families and civil dispute with regard to property is going on.

He further states that earlier also, an FIR was lodged at the instance of the applicant against the husband, father-in-law and mother-in-law of the informant and in sequence of the said, the FIR in question was lodged.
It is argued that the applicant is 75 years of age and in custody since 4.2.2023.
It is argued that only charge sheet has been filed and the trial has not even started.
5. Learned AGA has vehemently opposed the bail application.

6. Considering the submissions made at the bar, there is a huge variance in the statements of the victim in the FIR and statements under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. and the inherent improbabilities of the allegations, the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.

7. Let the applicant Indar be released on bail in Case Crime No.16 of 2023, under Section 376-AB,
504 IPC and Section 5M/6 of POCSO Act at P.S. Maurawan, District -Unnao on his furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 21.7.2023 -Amit K-
